tieuDeEn: School is more fun with friends – friendly competition keeps us keen. Love and respect good friends, and don't get too close to badly behaved ones. Teachers and good friends help us, but no one can learn for us – our own hard work matters most.

dichXuoi.en: At school we have teachers, and friends make it fun; competing with friends keeps us from getting bored. We love and respect good friends, and don't get too close to badly behaved ones.

dichXuoi.vi: Thầy dạy ta, ta phải biết ơn; có bạn hiền thì ta được giúp ích. Nhưng việc học không ai làm thay được – tự mình siêng năng là hơn cả.
dichXuoi.en: Our teachers teach us, so we must be grateful; good friends help us too. But no one can learn for us – our own hard work matters most.

Vì sao không nên thân thiết với bạn có thói xấu?
Vì sao tự mình siêng năng là quan trọng nhất?

baiHoc: Có bạn cùng thi đua, học không chán.
Yêu quý bạn hiền; đừng thân với bạn có thói xấu.
Không ai học thay mình – tự siêng năng là hơn cả.
baiHocEn: Studying with friends keeps learning fun. Love good friends and keep away from bad habits. No one can learn for you – your own hard work matters most.
viecTot: Tuần này, em rủ một bạn hiền cùng thi đua đọc sách hoặc làm bài, và tự ôn bài mỗi ngày không cần nhắc.
en: Cô Hà welcomes you to lesson thirty of “Lên Tám”. Today is a special milestone – we're halfway through this group of lessons. The poet Tản Đà will teach you how to choose friends at school and how to be independent and self-motivated in your learning every day. Listen carefully.
Learning from teachers is more fun with friends; competing with friends, we never get bored; good friends we love and respect; badly behaved friends we shouldn't get too close to.
Teachers teach us, and we're grateful; good friends help us too; but no one can do our learning for us – our own hard work matters most.

The poem paints a cheerful school: besides teachers teaching, the biggest joy of childhood is having friends your age to compete with and help each other improve. The poet also gives wise advice on choosing friends: good friends – hard-working, obedient and kind – we should love and learn from. With friends who are still lazy or naughty, keep some distance so their habits don't rub off on you.

Next, the poet sums up an important truth about doing things yourself: teachers teach you and good friends help and cheer you on, but no one can turn knowledge into your own for you. Whether you do well depends on your own effort. Being hard-working yourself is the key.
